study_identification.title: Social behavior in ASD males: The interplay between cognitive flexibility, working memory, and functional connectivity deviations

study_characteristics.study_objective: To evaluate whether individual deviations in between-network resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) map to social behavior in ASD males, and test whether executive functions (particularly cognitive flexibility and working memory) mediate these associations.

deviation_metric.answer: Individual z-scores calculated as: z = (actual FC - predicted FC) / SD_training, where predicted FC is from the normative GAM model and SD_training is the population standard deviation from the training dataset
deviation_metric.reason: The deviation score calculation is explicitly described with the formula provided in the methods section.
deviation_metric.supporting_text: Deviation scores (z) were then calculated by subtracting predicted between-network FC from actual between-network FC, and dividing the difference by the training dataset standard deviation (population standard deviation). These z scores reflect the individual degree of between-network FC atypicality from a typically developing population mean. Deviation Equation: zi = ( FCi - ̂ FCi ) / SD

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Sparse canonical correlation analysis (CCA) using PMA package v1.2.1 to identify associations between 21 between-network FC deviation scores and 5 SRS subscale scores; penalty determined via CCA.permute with 1000 permutations; best penalty L1=0.1 for both datasets; 5 canonical components extracted. Mediation analysis using mediation package v4.5.0 with 5000 bootstrap simulations to test whether BRIEF executive function scores (Global Executive Composite and 8 domain scores) mediated the association between between-network deviation scores and SRS total score; Bonferroni correction applied for 8 domains (adjusted alpha=0.00625). Mann-Whitney Wilcoxon tests for group differences in key deviation scores between ASD and non-ASD males. Sensitivity analyses performed controlling for full-scale IQ.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Between-network rsFC deviations in VAN-DMN, SMN-FPN, and VAN-FPN were significantly associated with distinct dimensions of social behavior in ASD males, with cognitive flexibility and working memory significantly mediating the VAN-DMN deviation to social behavior pathway.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Normative GAM trajectories for 21 between-network rsFC measures were trained on 321 non-ASD males and applied to 495 testing participants (77 non-ASD, 418 ASD). Sparse CCA identified five components linking deviation scores to social behavior: (1) VAN×DMN z-scores positively correlated with Social Awareness (r=0.272), (2) VAN×DMN with Social Communication (r=0.215), (3) SMN×FPN with Social Cognition (r=0.214), (4) VAN×FPN with Social Awareness (r=0.220, negative weights), and (5) VAN×DMN with Social Cognition (r=0.200). Group comparisons showed trending difference in VAN×DMN between ASD and controls (W=18109, p=0.081) but not for other features, highlighting heterogeneity. Mediation analysis (n=151 ASD with BRIEF data) showed BRIEF Global Executive Composite partially mediated VAN×DMN z to SRS total association (ACME=2.956, 95% CI [1.059, 5.4], p=0.0028; proportion mediated=0.473). Domain-level analyses revealed significant mediation for Cognitive Flexibility (ACME=2.839, p=0.0048, proportion=0.454) and Working Memory (ACME=2.258, p=0.0044, proportion=0.361) after Bonferroni correction (adjusted alpha=0.00625). Sensitivity analyses controlling for IQ showed similar results. Normative trajectories were largely linear across ages 5-14 years.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Cross-sectional design precludes developmental causal inference and significantly underestimates actual longitudinal changes (Di Biase et al., 2023); single-domain dataset (ABIDE) without external validation limits generalizability; male-only cohort prevents examination of sex differences in functional connectivity deviations; imbalanced age distribution (majority 9-12 years) limits applicability across all childhood phases; lack of standard normative modeling performance metrics (EV, MSLL) on test controls; potential unmeasured confounders in mediation analysis; inability to establish whether brain connectivity atypicality is causal or consequential to ASD behavioral pathology; ComBat harmonization may risk information distortion; lack of clinical specificity testing (findings may apply to other neurodevelopmental disorders); genetic and environmental factors not considered in prediction error assessment; no examination of subtypes via clustering algorithms.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Study demonstrates feasibility of individual-level between-network rsFC deviation quantification in ASD males using normative modeling. Findings highlight cognitive flexibility and working memory as potential intervention targets to improve social outcomes in ASD males, though validation in independent cohorts is needed. Authors suggest normative modeling is well-suited for heterogeneous conditions like ASD, as it characterizes individual-level heterogeneity rather than seeking an 'average patient' pattern. Future directions include: (1) prospective longitudinal studies to calibrate cross-sectional models; (2) extending to ASD females given distinct neuroimaging patterns; (3) balanced age distribution to examine associations across developmental phases; (4) focus on early life (first few years) to establish biomarker precedence; (5) applying clustering algorithms to identify subtypes based on deviation patterns.

general_notes.general_notes: Dataset details: ABIDE I and II (N=2226 total) restricted to males aged 5.1-14.0 years (N=816); Training/test split: 80/20 for non-ASD males (321 training, 77 testing), all ASD males in testing (418). Network parcellation: Yeo 7-network (VN, SMN, DAN, VAN, LN, FPN, DMN) yielding 21 between-network edges. Harmonization: ComBat across 18 batches based on site + scan parameters (neuroCombat v1.0.13); batch effects significantly reduced (Supplementary Tables 3a-b). GAM specification: y ~ s(ScanAge, k=variable, bs='tp') + QC_meanmotion; family=gaussian; method=REML; k and edf values vary by feature (Supplementary Table 4). Behavioral measures: SRS (5 subscales: Awareness, Communication, Cognition, Motivation, Mannerisms) T-scores used; BRIEF (8 domains + GEC) T-scores used. Statistical software: R v4.3.0; mgcv v1.8-42; PMA v1.2.1; mediation v4.5.0. Multi-site details: 18 sites across ABIDE I and II with varying scanners (Siemens TrioTim, GE MR750, GE Signa, Philips Achieva, Siemens Allegra, Philips Intera, Siemens Verio) and acquisition parameters (Supplementary Table 2). Study emphasizes precision medicine approach to dissect ASD heterogeneity at individual level, moving beyond group-average case-control designs.
